content.text: Excellent — the equivalence test caught a real regression (`null` is valid JSON that parses to `None`, which my sentinel conflated with failure). Fixing:

arguments.command:
cd /workspace/submission && python3 - <<'EOF'
src = open('ipv6_replay.py').read()
src = src.replace('''def parse_row_json(text):
    """Decode one response row.

    Returns (obj, schema_prechecked).  obj is None when the row fails the
    json level checks.  schema_prechecked means the object already passed
    every schema level check, so the caller can skip re-validation.

    A row whose text contains no escape and exactly ROW_QUOTE_COUNT quote
    characters cannot hide a duplicate key or a nonfinite number once the
    decoded object has exactly the expected keys with the expected value
    types: every key and string value is then spelled literally, once, and
    any float (finite or not) would fail the integer type checks.
    """
    if text.count('"') == ROW_QUOTE_COUNT and "\\\\" not in text:
        try:
            obj = json.loads(text)
        except ValueError:
            return None, False
        if (type(obj) is dict and len(obj) == 6 and obj.keys() == ROW_KEYS
                and type(obj["probe_id"]) is str
                and type(obj["target"]) is str
                and type(obj["source"]) is str
                and type(obj["received_ms"]) is int
                and type(obj["type"]) is int
                and type(obj["code"]) is int
                and obj["probe_id"]
                and len(obj["probe_id"]) <= MAX_PROBE_ID_LEN):
            return obj, True
        # Fall through and classify the row exactly with the strict decoder.
    try:
        return decode_json_strict(text), False
    except (ValueError, RecursionError):
        return None, False''',
'''def parse_row_json(text):
    """Decode one response row.

    Returns (json_reason, obj, schema_prechecked).  json_reason is "json" or
    None; obj is the decoded value (which may be any JSON value, including
    None).  schema_prechecked means the object already passed every schema
    level check, so the caller can skip re-validation.

    A row whose text contains no escape and exactly ROW_QUOTE_COUNT quote
    characters cannot hide a duplicate key or a nonfinite number once the
    decoded object has exactly the expected keys with the expected value
    types: every key and string value is then spelled literally, once, and
    any float (finite or not) would fail the integer type checks.
    """
    if text.count('"') == ROW_QUOTE_COUNT and "\\\\" not in text:
        try:
            obj = json.loads(text)
        except ValueError:
            return "json", None, False
        if (type(obj) is dict and len(obj) == 6 and obj.keys() == ROW_KEYS
                and type(obj["probe_id"]) is str
                and type(obj["target"]) is str
                and type(obj["source"]) is str
                and type(obj["received_ms"]) is int
                and type(obj["type"]) is int
                and type(obj["code"]) is int
                and obj["probe_id"]
                and len(obj["probe_id"]) <= MAX_PROBE_ID_LEN):
            return None, obj, True
        # Fall through and classify the row exactly with the strict decoder.
    try:
        return None, decode_json_strict(text), False
    except (ValueError, RecursionError):
        return "json", None, False''')
src = src.replace('''        try:
            text = raw.decode("utf-8")
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            reason = "json"
        else:
            obj, prechecked = parse_row_json(text)
            if obj is None:
                reason = "json"
        if reason is None and not prechecked:''',
